newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba to launch new electronic bidding system.
newsitem.headline: Buba to launch new electronic bidding system.

text.p: The Bundesbank plans to launch an electronic bidding system next week which will signifantly cut down the time it takes the central bank to award funds to banks, a senior Bundesbank official said.

"We plan to launch a new system which will speed up settlements and vastly improve security for banks bidding for funds in the weekly securities repurchase tender at the central bank," Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke told foreign journalists.

With the new system, dubbed ABS for automated bidding system, banks will have an electronic link to their state central banks, able to place bids in government auctions, or the weekly Bundesbank repo tender in split seconds, Welteke said.
Welteke, who is also president in the state central bank in Hesse, praised the system as one more step to make Frankfurt into a leading financial centre.
Currently, banks contact their central banks either via phone or fax and it takes the Bundesbank considerably longer to calculate the weekly tender awards.
"Soon traders, like money market traders, will know within a few minutes not hours how much liquidity they will be awarded," Welteke explained to foreign journalists.
The new system will be launched first in the state of Hesse, home to Germany's financial capital Frankfurt and up to 160 banks could participate, Welteke said.
Welteke said there were about 160 banks in the state the could take part in auctions and, some 80 banks participated on a regular basis.
Once the system passes its initial test, it is expected to be launched in other states as well.
